source: Reiter (1987) A theory of diagnosis from first principles
finding: Founding theory. A system is (SD, COMPONENTS, OBS). A diagnosis is a minimal set of components whose being abnormal (rest normal) makes SD + OBS consistent. The PDF is a scanned image with no text layer, so it could not be read this session. Content below is known only through Greiner et al. (a02) and later papers that quote it.
numbers: 39 page scan, 1.75 MB, CCITT images; no OCR tool available
limits: Not read. Treat any claim attributed to Reiter in this file as second-hand unless the line cites a paper that was opened.
agent_relevance: Primary source still unread; a later pass should OCR it before we cite exact wording.

source: Greiner, Smith, Wilkerson (1989) A correction to the algorithm in Reiter's theory of diagnosis
finding: States the core result: a set is a diagnosis if and only if it is a minimal hitting set of the collection of conflict sets (Reiter Theorem 4.4). A conflict set is a set of components that cannot all be normal given SD and OBS. Reiter finds minimal hitting sets by building an HS-tree whose node labels are conflicts returned by a theorem prover.
numbers: Theorem 1 = Reiter 1987 Theorem 4.4. Counterexample collection {{a,b},{b,c},{a,c},{b,d},{b}} loses the minimal hitting set {a,b} under Reiter's pruning.
quote: components is a diagnosis ... if and only if it is a minimal hitting set for the collection of conflict sets
limits: Note covers only the hitting-set algorithm, not the logic of the full theory.
agent_relevance: Gives the exact mapping we can use in S5: each failed check yields a conflict (set of steps or assumptions that cannot all be right); the fault candidates are the minimal hitting sets of those conflicts.

source: Greiner, Smith, Wilkerson (1989) A correction to the algorithm in Reiter's theory of diagnosis
finding: Reiter's published HS-tree algorithm was wrong. Three pruning ideas interact badly: reusing node labels, closing nodes, and removing redundant edges when a subset conflict is found. The pruned tree can lose minimal hitting sets, so some true diagnoses are missed. The fix replaces the tree by a directed acyclic graph (HS-DAG) with node reuse and relabelling, plus a proof of correctness.
numbers: Failing example has 5 conflict sets over 4 components (a,b,c,d). Two small examples (Fig 1, Fig 2) show lost diagnoses and the need to relabel pruned nodes.
quote: Reiter's description of the algorithm is incorrect in that some diagnoses can be missed under certain conditions
limits: A 1989 note; later work (Wotawa 2001 and others) revised the algorithm again; not read here.
agent_relevance: Warns that a hand-rolled conflict-to-candidate step with pruning can silently drop the true culprit. If we compute hitting sets in code we must test completeness against brute force on small cases.

source: Greiner, Smith, Wilkerson (1989) A correction to the algorithm in Reiter's theory of diagnosis
finding: Reiter's method accepts non-minimal conflict sets; de Kleer and Williams' method needs the underlying inference engine to deliver only minimal conflicts. Conflicts are computed on demand by a theorem prover and each call is expensive, so the algorithm is built to minimise prover calls.
numbers: none (design statement)
limits: Description of two 1987 papers as seen by the 1989 note.
agent_relevance: Our code-run check plays the theorem prover. Each check is costly (tokens or sandbox time), so reuse of earlier conflicts to label new nodes is the right design pressure.

source: de Kleer, Williams (1987) Diagnosing multiple faults
finding: GDE (General Diagnostic Engine). Predictions come from component models; a discrepancy yields conflicts, i.e. minimal sets of assumptions (components working) that cannot all hold. Candidates are the minimal sets of components that intersect every conflict. An ATMS records which assumptions each prediction depends on. Candidates are ranked by probability and the next measurement is chosen to cut entropy. Full text was not reachable (host refused or timed out), so this is second-hand via a06, a07, a09.
numbers: abstract only seen in search snippet: tested on digital-circuit troubleshooting
limits: Not read. Details such as prior probabilities and the worked example are unverified.
agent_relevance: Blueprint for S5 plus S7: conflicts from failed checks, candidate faults as hitting sets, rank them, pick the next test by information gain.

source: Stern, Kalech, Feldman, Provan (2012) Exploring the duality in conflict-directed model-based diagnosis
finding: Describes the classical pipeline as two NP-hard steps: compute minimal conflicts, then compute minimal hitting sets. GDE used an ATMS to manage and minimise conflict generation. Probabilities were later used to focus search on likely conflicts (de Kleer and Williams 1989). Conflict-directed A* (Williams and Ragno 2007) uses fault probabilities for best-first hitting-set search over an incrementally generated conflict set.
numbers: Counts of possible conflicts and diagnoses are always exponential in the number of components (their statement).
quote: conflict-based diagnosis actually has to solve two NP-hard problems
limits: Authors' own framing, written to motivate their new algorithm.
agent_relevance: Tells us what to expect: exact enumeration will not scale, so for an agent keep fault sets very small (single and double faults) and use probability-ordered search.

source: Stern, Kalech, Feldman, Provan (2012) Exploring the duality in conflict-directed model-based diagnosis
finding: Proves a duality: a diagnosis is a hitting set of the conflicts, and a conflict is a hitting set of the diagnoses. Their algorithm (SDE) alternates: current diagnoses steer the search for new conflicts, current conflicts steer the search for diagnoses. It stops when no new hitting set of the conflicts exists.
numbers: Fraction of instances where a minimal-cardinality diagnosis was found within 30 s, CDA* vs SDE: 74283 100% vs 99%; 74182 100% vs 100%; 74181 47% vs 79%; c432 33% vs 88%; c499 9% vs 30%; c880 5% vs 14%; c1355 0% vs 9%. Observations per system 76 to 350. On larger ISCAS85 circuits CDA* solved none.
limits: Single lab, benchmark circuits, 30 s limit, task = one minimum-cardinality diagnosis. Orthogonal speed-ups (cones, fast hitting set) not applied.
agent_relevance: Supports a two-way loop for the agent: use the current best suspects to choose the next check, and use each failed check to prune suspects. Gain grows with fault cardinality.

source: de Kleer, Mackworth, Reiter (1992) Characterizing diagnoses and systems
finding: Shows minimal diagnosis is inadequate when components also have fault models, because a superset of a faulty set need not be a diagnosis. Proposes kernel diagnosis (prime implicants of the conflict set) instead. Defines a conflict as an AB-clause entailed by SD plus OBS; most earlier work used only positive conflicts, i.e. sets of components that cannot all be normal. Minimal diagnoses of weak-fault models are the minimal hitting sets of the minimal positive conflicts.
numbers: Theorems 1 to 12; no experiments (theory paper). OCR of the opened copy is garbled, so wording is partly reconstructed.
quote: not every superset of the faulty components of a diagnosis necessarily provides a diagnosis
limits: Text layer noisy; only abstract, definitions and theorem statements checked.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: minimal-hitting-set reasoning works when we model only the correct behaviour of steps. If our agent also models how a step can fail (strong fault models), plain minimal sets mislead; keep the fault vocabulary weak and simple.

source: Siddiqi, Huang (2011) Sequential diagnosis by abstraction
finding: GDE proposes the measurement that cuts the Shannon entropy of the distribution over computed diagnoses the most, on average. Reported earlier results (de Kleer et al. 1992) on ISCAS-85 single faults give costs close to optimal policies. Drawback: with many diagnoses it is impractical, and using only a few probable diagnoses raises the average number of measurements.
numbers: Comparison with tutorial GDE on small ISCAS subcircuits (50 circuits each of sizes 13, 14, 15, 16 and 10 of size 17; 5 single, 5 double, 5 triple fault scenarios each). Mean measurements are similar, e.g. size 13 single-fault 3.6 (gde) vs 3.6 (sda); but gde time grows from 2.0 s (size 13) to 2876 s (size 17) while sda stays at 0.01 s. Tutorial gde could not solve any full ISCAS-85 circuit. Fault prior used: P(ok)=0.9 per gate.
limits: The gde used was a tutorial version computing minimal, not probable, diagnoses; comparison is on small subcircuits only.
agent_relevance: Entropy-based test choice is accurate but costly to compute; a cheap proxy that avoids enumerating all candidates keeps the same number of tests. Our S7 can use a proxy score.

source: Siddiqi, Huang (2011) Sequential diagnosis by abstraction
finding: Random measurement order is much worse than informed order, and knowing the fault cardinality helps a lot. On circuit c432 (160 gates) the random strategy needs far more measurements than the entropy-guided heuristic.
numbers: c432 mean measurements, single-fault: random 92.3 without pruning vs 4.5 with cardinality pruning; with no pruning sda(ew) 42.0. Double-fault: random 97.7 no pruning, 36.8 with pruning; sda(ew) 42.5 no pruning.
limits: Table partially read; only c432 rows checked. Circuits are combinational digital logic.
agent_relevance: The value of a good probe order and a fault-count prior is large (about 20x on one case). Suggests the agent should declare a single-fault assumption by default and drop it only on evidence.

source: Grastien, Haslum, Thiebaux (2023) A more general theory of diagnosis from first principles
finding: Generalises Reiter beyond set-of-faults to any hypothesis space with a preference order. A conflict is any object that stands for a set of hypotheses proven not to contain the diagnosis; it can be larger than the hypothesis tested. Reiter's search is preferred-first and uses conflicts to skip successors. The set space is finite and a lattice, which made Reiter's algorithm simple; richer spaces (multisets, sequences of faults) break these properties.
numbers: Power-grid style benchmark: 129 instances, 2 to 146 alarms, up to 10,000 components in the network. Second benchmark: 300-instance set. Hardness order matches theory: fewer solved for sequence space than multiset than set space.
quote: a conflict is a chunk of the hypothesis space ... that is proven to contain no candidate
limits: Discrete-event systems; not about language agents. Time limit 1800 s on the first benchmark.
agent_relevance: A failed attempt rules out a whole region of explanations, not one: the right record for each failure is the set of assumptions it refutes. Candidate spaces for reasoning are not plain sets (order of steps matters), so their generalisation is the one to borrow.

source: Grastien, Haslum, Thiebaux (2023) A more general theory of diagnosis from first principles
finding: Reports how conflict use helps. On the 129-instance benchmark the junction-tree method solves only 23. Preferred-first search with conflicts and a SAT test solver solves 12 more instances than a BDD method and 4 more with a heuristic-search solver; the instances it fails are failed by every method. Preferred-first search returns valid minimal candidates even when it times out.
numbers: JT solves 23 of 129. pfs+ec/SAT solves 12 more than BDD; pfs with heuristic-search solver 4 more than BDD; BDD solves 9 more than pls. In 17% of unsolved-but-known cases the partial pls candidate set already equalled the full minimal diagnosis; only the last proof step failed.
limits: Single benchmark family; time limit 1800 s.
agent_relevance: Anytime behaviour matters: ranked candidates found early are usually already right, and only the proof of completeness is expensive. For the agent, act on the top candidate and skip the completeness proof.

source: Grastien, Haslum, Thiebaux (2023) A more general theory of diagnosis from first principles
finding: Explains the relation to de Kleer and Williams: Reiter models only correct behaviour (weak fault models), so supersets of a candidate are also candidates and the minimal set represents all. De Kleer and Williams allow faulty-behaviour models (strong), where this fails, and use an ATMS but still the set space. Kernel diagnosis was introduced to keep a compact representation.
numbers: none
limits: Authors' survey of lineage.
agent_relevance: Keeps the lineage straight for our write-up: Reiter 1987 = logic and hitting sets; GDE 1987 = ATMS plus probabilities plus measurements; KMR 1992 = kernel diagnoses.

source: Roos (1993) Efficient model based diagnosis
finding: Uses causal structure: the conflict set of a wrong output is only the components its predicted value actually depends on (a dependency set), and confirming measurements shrink or cancel components. Gives rules to focus on components that appear in the most conflict sets, with fault probabilities updated by Bayes. Both steps (choose focus, choose probe) cost O(n^2) in the worst case and linear when connectivity is low.
numbers: Worst case O(n^2) in the number of components n; linear with low connectivity. No empirical tables found in text.
quote: a set of focuses on likely broken components is determined ... the most informative probing point within the focus
limits: Theory paper with small examples; also notes that choosing the minimum number of components to hit all conflicts is as hard as minimum hitting set.
agent_relevance: Shows how to cut conflict size using real dependence: only steps whose output the wrong result actually depends on belong in the conflict. This matches our rule to cite the actual failing output (G2).

source: Rodler (2020) DynamicHS: streamlining Reiter's hitting-set tree for sequential diagnosis
finding: In sequential diagnosis the HS-tree was rebuilt after each new measurement. DynamicHS keeps the tree between iterations and reuses it, answering a question Reiter raised in 1987 about reusing a tree when new information arrives. It keeps all HS-tree guarantees.
numbers: On real knowledge-base diagnosis problems: less time than HS-Tree in 96% of sessions; median saving 52%, maximum 75%; in the hardest cases it avoided median and maximum overheads of over 175% and 800%. Saving did not depend on the number of fault explanations or on the measurement heuristic. Hard reasoner calls took 4 to over 100 times longer than easy ones.
limits: Domain is ontology and knowledge-base debugging, where reasoner calls dominate cost; results are time, not number of measurements.
agent_relevance: Persist the candidate structure across rounds; do not recompute from scratch after each new test. Cost is in the expensive checks, so reuse earlier conflicts.

source: Orvalho, Kwiatkowska, Janota, Manquinho (2025) Model-based diagnosis with multiple observations: CFaults
finding: Applies consistency-based diagnosis to C programs: each statement is a component with an 'abnormal' switch, failing tests are observations, and one MaxSAT formula covers all failing tests at once so diagnoses are consistent across every observation and are subset-minimal. Per-test methods that merge minimal sets later can blow up memory or give redundant diagnoses.
numbers: CFaults localises faults in 31% more programs than BugAssist, 36% more than SNIPER and 15% more than HSD on C-Pack-IPAs. TCAS: 41 programs, up to 131 failing tests each; SNIPER hits the 32 GB memory limit on 73% (30 of 41). BugAssist gave a non-optimal diagnosis in 2.4% of cases. ISCAS85: slower than HSD but localises faults in only 6% fewer circuits.
limits: Authors' own tool and benchmarks; C-Pack-IPAs results use the 48% of programs that pass pre-filtering.
agent_relevance: Strong precedent for our case: aggregate ALL failing outputs into one joint consistency problem before localising, instead of reasoning test by test.

source: Orvalho, Janota, Manquinho (2024/2025) Counterexample guided program repair using zero-shot learning and MaxSAT-based fault localization
finding: A model-based diagnosis step finds the buggy statements (MaxSAT fault localisation, as in CFaults). The LLM then receives the program with those statements blanked as a sketch, and fills them in a counterexample-guided loop. This keeps repairs small, which plain LLM repair often does not.
numbers: 1,431 incorrect student C programs. Best portfolio of 6 open LLMs (no reference implementation): 1013 repaired, 70.8%. Best single model across configs: 59.1%; with sketches plus description and tests: up to 48.3%. Symbolic baselines in 90 s: CLARA 495 (34.6%), VERIFIX 91 (6.3%). Loop used 1.14 iterations on average, max 7; 89% fixed on first attempt. With a reference implementation added, one table cell reached 1190 (83.2%).
limits: Small open 7B-class models, student programs, no comparison against an LLM given no localisation hint at equal budget shown in the passages read; reference implementation changes edit size.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence that a diagnosis step which tells the model WHERE to look and leaves a hole to fill helps small models. Fits S5 (locate by code, model fixes).

source: He, Kirschbaum, Kasiviswanathan (2026) Global consistency repair for natural-language claim sets (QXR)
finding: Uses the Reiter pipeline almost literally with an LLM as the consistency oracle. It finds minimal unsatisfiable subsets of claims with QuickXplain, collects them as conflicts, then deletes a greedy hitting set. Direct all-at-once LLM judging over-prunes: it detects inconsistency but removes too many claims.
numbers: VitaminC: 24 to 32 claims per case, 2 to 6 injected contradictions; mean 4.05 MUSes and minimum hitting set size 4.05. FEVER: 33.7 claims, 4.77 MUSes, hitting set 4.01. Recall of kept valid claims on VitaminC: Claude Sonnet 4.5 0.617 direct vs 0.957 QXR; Claude Opus 4.6 0.574 vs 0.968. RAMDocs (30 claims, 10 gold conflicts): Qwen2.5-7B F1 0.741 to 0.815; 32B 0.845 to 0.920; Haiku 4.5 0.724 to 0.863; Sonnet 4.5 0.882 to 0.870; DeepSeek-V4-Pro 0.861 to 0.904.
limits: Pairwise-checking all claims would need 435 oracle calls at N=30 and 4,950 at N=100. Gains are small or absent where direct judging is already strong (FEVER, Sonnet 4.5 on RAMDocs). Oracle errors are assumed rare in the proofs; v2 dated 2026-10-09, not peer reviewed.
agent_relevance: Most direct match in the literature to our idea. A model asked to repair a whole set at once over-deletes; localise small conflicts first, then take a hitting set in code.

source: He, Kirschbaum, Kasiviswanathan (2026) Global consistency repair for natural-language claim sets (QXR)
finding: Proves repair equals hitting set: a deletion restores consistency exactly when it hits every minimal inconsistent subset (Theorem A.2). Pairwise checks are provably insufficient (a graph-colouring construction gives a set where every pair is consistent but the whole is not). Greedy hitting set has the usual set-cover guarantee. Exact localisation costs O(k log N) oracle queries with QuickXplain.
numbers: k = size of a conflict, N = number of claims; information bound needs at least log2 of the number of possible conflicts queries.
limits: Guarantees assume a correct oracle; with a noisy LLM judge they hold only approximately, which the paper says openly.
agent_relevance: Gives a cost model and a correctness argument for a conflict-then-hitting-set step; confirms we should never rely on pairwise contradiction checks alone.

source: Singh, Cassel, Weir, Feng, Bayless (2026) VERGE: formal refinement and guidance engine for verifiable LLM reasoning
finding: Breaks an LLM answer into atomic claims, formalises them in logic, checks with an SMT solver, and feeds back a Minimal Correction Subset (the smallest set of claims to drop to restore consistency) rather than a raw unsat core. Ablation shows the minimal-correction feedback matters most on strict constraint tasks.
numbers: With GPT-OSS-120B: average +18.7% over single-pass at convergence. Ablation (Full vs without MCS): FOLIO 84.7 vs 80.7, ProofWriter 89.9 vs 88.7, ZebraLogic 91.0 vs 88.9; AR-LSAT 91.7 down to 83.0 without MCS. Feedback types on FOLIO: Full 84.7, soft-only 80.8, unsat-core-only 79.3, minimal-solver-feedback 76.5. Humanities Last Exam 14.2% (chain of thought) to 30.5%; HLE falls to 15.2% when routing is removed.
limits: Authors' own ablation on a few benchmarks, one main model; gains partly from iteration itself; v3 dated 2026-10-11 and not peer reviewed. The MCS and unsat-core feedback share a minimal-set idea but VERGE does not build a diagnosis over many failed attempts.
agent_relevance: Shows that feeding the model the minimal part to change (hitting-set style) beats feeding the whole failing core, at least on logic tasks. Supports a revision prompt that names the smallest suspect set.

source: Wassermann (2000) Local diagnosis
finding: Links consistency-based diagnosis to belief revision (kernel semi-revision): a conflict is a minimal inconsistent subset (a kernel) of the system description plus observation, and a diagnosis removes a hitting set of the kernels. Proposes first isolating the part of the description relevant to the observation, then diagnosing only that part.
numbers: none (theory, 2000, 10 Mar)
limits: Short theory paper; no experiments; only introduction read closely.
agent_relevance: Same structure as our case: conflict = minimal inconsistent subset of beliefs; repair = hitting set. Local focus before diagnosis reduces cost, as in QXR scopes.

source: DX 2025 (Dagstuhl OASIcs vol 136) Are diagnostic concepts within the reach of LLMs?
finding: Page abstract read, full PDF not read. Asks LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, o1, o3-mini) to generate Minimal Structurally Overdetermined sets (equation subsets that give diagnosis tests) for hybrid dynamic systems and Boolean circuits, and compares with the Fault Diagnosis Toolbox; then computes diagnoses from the generated sets. Keywords list conflicts and diagnoses.
numbers: Abstract page gives no metrics; PDF is 20 pages.
limits: Only abstract seen; authors not recorded. Treat as pointer, not evidence of accuracy.
agent_relevance: Shows the diagnosis community is testing whether LLMs can produce the conflict-like objects themselves; our design keeps that step in code, which this line suggests is the safer choice until the numbers are read.

source: Stern, Kalech, Feldman, Provan (2012) Exploring the duality in conflict-directed model-based diagnosis
finding: Notes two drawbacks of conflict-based diagnosis. Completeness: most approaches use sound but incomplete conflict generation, so they cannot find all conflicts. Cost: even computing minimal conflicts is NP-hard. Authors still keep a conflict-driven design because conflicts prune whole regions.
numbers: Fig 2: advantage of SDE over CDA* grows with diagnosis cardinality (30 s limit, 74XXX and small ISCAS85 circuits).
limits: Argument is the authors'; benchmark circuits only.
agent_relevance: Boundary: conflicts found by sampling or heuristics are incomplete, so the true culprit can be missing from the hitting-set list. Keep an 'other / unknown' candidate in the ranking.

source: Siddiqi, Huang (2011) Sequential diagnosis by abstraction
finding: Reports the GDE design choice that all measurements have unit cost, so the objective is the fewest measurements. Also reports a trade-off from de Kleer (1992): more computed diagnoses make the heuristic more accurate; a short list of probable ones is faster but raises average cost.
numbers: no exact figure beyond a09/a10
limits: Secondary account of GDE; primary not read.
agent_relevance: Trade-off for design: how many candidate explanations to carry. Small list is cheap but risks irrelevant probes; keep the top few plus an unexplored mass.

source: Reiter (1987) A theory of diagnosis from first principles; as quoted in Grastien et al. (2023)
finding: Reiter's own algorithm 'diagnose' is a preferred-first search that uses conflicts from a theorem prover to skip candidates. Note from the opened Grastien paper that the set hypothesis space made the specialised implementation possible. The original text itself was not read.
numbers: none
limits: Second-hand through a11.
agent_relevance: Same as a02; kept as a separate line so the unread status of the primary is visible.

source: Williams, Ragno (2007) Conflict-directed A* and its role in model-based embedded systems
finding: Conflict-directed A* searches states best-first by probability and removes subspaces around each inconsistent state found. Used for fault isolation, mode estimation, repair and model-based programming. Seen only in a search-result summary; the paper was not opened.
numbers: Stern et al. (a07) report it solves 0% of c1355 instances under 30 s versus 9% for SDE, and none on larger ISCAS85 circuits.
limits: Result is from a competitor's benchmark, not the authors'.
agent_relevance: Best-first over probable candidates with conflict-based pruning is the standard way to produce a ranked list; relevant for ranking by probability in S7.

source: He, Kirschbaum, Kasiviswanathan (2026) Global consistency repair for natural-language claim sets (QXR)
finding: Reports the limits. The method pays extra oracle calls and wins only when the set is mostly coherent with a few local conflicts; where direct judging is already reliable (FEVER, some strong models) gains shrink or reverse. Weighted deletion cost and a graded (probability) oracle are listed as future work, not tested.
numbers: Sonnet 4.5 on RAMDocs: F1 0.882 direct vs 0.870 QXR (slightly worse). Qwen2.5-7B VitaminC-style gains larger than for strong models, suggesting structure compensates for weak set-level reasoning.
limits: Single paper, version 2; no human check of oracle errors.
agent_relevance: Apply the conflict step only when a check has failed and the candidate set is large (G1, G12); on easy items it adds cost with no gain (G7).

source: Orvalho, Kwiatkowska, Janota, Manquinho (2025) Model-based diagnosis with multiple observations: CFaults
finding: Documents a failure of per-test fault localisation: merging the minimal correction sets computed separately for each failing test can exhaust memory and does not guarantee a diagnosis consistent across all tests. Their remedy replicates the program once per failing test inside one MaxSAT formula that shares the 'abnormal' variables.
numbers: SNIPER: memory limit (32 GB) reached on 73% of TCAS programs, up to 131 failing tests per program. TCAS has about 180 lines.
limits: Memory-out is partly an implementation property of SNIPER.
agent_relevance: Warns against diagnosing each failed attempt separately and then intersecting; share the suspect variables across all attempts.
